chapter: Jazz at the Philharmonic and later years
title: Continuing his group after Joe Williams: quartet in New York
summary: He kept Forrest with new pianists and drummers, then worked quartet jobs at the Arpeggio Room, Embers and Roundtable.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, let's go back now. What happened after you broke up this group then, with Joe?
Joe? I continued on with the group. I got Hugh Lawson . He played piano with me. And had the same group. Not Elvin, but I had Clarence -- he was a drummer, used to be with Dizzy. Clarence Johnson.
He continued on with me until I disbanded the band, you know. But that's --
And Jimmy Forrest was still with you?
Jimmy Forrest stayed with me until the very end, you know. Then I started doing a quartet thing, too, worked in the Arpeggio Room in New York.
Oh, that was the time when Jonah's thing was....trumpet quartets.
Yes, yes and -- I mean, the -- what was the place there -- Jonah played there all the time.
The Embers. Started going to the Embers and started going to the Roundtable and, you know, I just worked all around New York with a quartet for a while, you know, after
